text:
oncall-bot: PAGERDUTY: P1 - GPU pool hotpath-south is saturated, queue length > 12k, 429s rising. Auto-escalation to oncall.
alice: i'm on it. seeing spikes in queue and immediate 429s from the tier policy layer. throwing pages for customer-facing endpoints. :rotating_light:
ben: logs show token_bucket rejects at routing:prod-standard tier. sample:
```
[2026-03-15T12:14:02Z] reject request id=tx-8d3 token_used=1 token_left=0 bucket=prod-standard reason=rate_exceeded
```
ben: autoscaler attempted to scale but failed repeatedly with scale error "quota_exceeded: gpu_global_capacity". looks like we hit a global upper bound, not pool min/max.
jin: confirmed. autoscaler logs:
```
scale_attempt: pool=hotpath-south desired=12 current=8 error=quota_exceeded(code=4295)
```
jin: also found an older tokenbucket config change from last week that set burst=120 and refill=30/s for prod-standard — that is too constrained for sudden prefix-caching misses.
sam: impact matrix? which customers are seeing 429s vs degraded latency?
maria: quick check: 8% of requests in prod-region-south saw 429s between 12:12-12:26 UTC. heavy hits on chat endpoints and long-sequence inference. affected customers: [acme-corp, pilot-inc, beta-shop].
alice: immediate plan:
1) widen token_bucket burst for prod-standard to 2000 (to allow short bursts)
2) add emergency routing to spillover-pool (best-effort, lower tier) for non-SLA traffic
3) request quota bump / temporary override for autoscaler to bypass global cap
4) post-incident follow-up to revert if needed
ben: i'm skeptical about quota bump speed. we should do config changes first (token bucket + routing) so requests can drain while we talk to infra for capacity.
alice: agreed. applying tokenbucket patch now.
```
# executing
redwoodctl config patch tier prod-standard --set token_bucket.burst=2000 --set token_bucket.refill_per_sec=200
```
ops-bot: config-patch accepted, version=cfg-2026-03-15T12:16Z, initiating rollout
ops-bot: canary on 2 nodes started
alice: enabling spillover rule to route lower-priority customers to spillover-pool:
```
routing_policy:
  name: emergency-spill
  match: request.metadata.priority != "sla"
  action: route_to: spillover-pool
```
ops-bot: routing rule applied (id=rr-981). starting immediate traffic split 95/5 to spillover.
sam: i'm toggling non-SLA flag for beta-shop test traffic to verify. pinging @maria for metrics.
maria: metrics after changes:
- queue length: 12k -> 3.4k within 7 mins
- 429 rate: 8% -> 1.1% over 8 mins
- tail latency (p99): 3.2s -> 1.8s
alice: nice. but still seeing autoscaler errors when it tries to add GPUs. need infra to lift global cap; paging infra-team.
ben: I'm creating emergency ticket with infra quotas and linking logs, requesting temporary override for 2h.
ben: ticket #INC-20260315-1947 created, assigned to infra-quota. contact: @jin infra.
jin: infra responded — they can grant a soft quota for 2h if we provide a list of pools and expected spike. sending details.
alice: prepping customer communication draft. cc @maria for numbers. proposal: 5% credit plus incident summary for affected customers.
maria: agree on credit. also suggest proactive config change: increase prod-standard refill to 300/s and add automatic burst scaling when queue_per_gpu > 500.
sam: suggestion accepted. but that needs prod rollout and tests.
alice: for now we keep emergency spill routing and increased burst. monitoring closely. oncall handoff in 30m to follow-up shift: will hand to @ben.
oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: from alice -> ben at 12:45 UTC. Incident status: mitigated, partial customer impact, action items created.
ben: taking handoff. notes: tokenbucket widened (burst=2000 refill=200/s), routing spillover active, infra ticket open for quota override. next steps: ensure autoscaler can actually add nodes after infra change, run a controlled canary for full rollback path.
jin: will coordinate with infra for quota. i'll try for faster lift; otherwise we may need to prewarm GPUs in a different region and route.
alice: thanks team. quick checklist posted to the incident board. will collect logs and timeline for postmortem. tagging follow-ups: root cause analysis for why tokenbucket was tightened last week, validate alert thresholds, and add playbook for spillover routing.
maria: attaching customer-impact spreadsheet here (summary, ids, affected times). will send to support to triage refunds.
ops-bot: incident updated: status=mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to P2 for follow-up work.
ben: leaving final note on thread before handoff: keep routing until autoscaler confirmed. don't revert tokenbucket until refill auto-scale is in place.
alice: handing over. good job everyone :thumbsup:
